statement: Let n = len(locations) and M = 1000000007. A route is a finite sequence of indices c_0, ..., c_m for some m >= 0 such that c_0 = start, c_m = finish, every c_t satisfies 0 <= c_t < n, c_t != c_{t+1} for every 0 <= t < m, and sum_{t=1..m} |locations[c_t] - locations[c_{t-1}]| <= fuel. The case m = 0 is the one-term sequence (start) and is allowed exactly when start = finish. Let C be the number of such routes. The function returns a result r and r = C mod M, i.e., r is the unique integer with 0 <= r < M and C ≡ r (mod M).
preconditions: len(locations) is between 2 and 100 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(locations), locations[i] is an integer with 1 <= locations[i] <= 1000000000; the values locations[i] are pairwise distinct; 0 <= start < len(locations); 0 <= finish < len(locations); 1 <= fuel <= 200.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail due to overflow, panic, or out-of-bounds access.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r < 1000000007.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if |locations[start] - locations[finish]| > fuel, then r = 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if for every j with 0 <= j < len(locations) and j != start we have |locations[j] - locations[start]| > fuel, then r = 1 when start = finish, and r = 0 when start != finish.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if start = finish and fuel < 2 * min { |locations[j] - locations[start]| : 0 <= j < len(locations), j != start }, then r = 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if for every pair of indices i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(locations) we have 2 * |locations[i] - locations[j]| > fuel, then r equals 1 when start = finish; if start != finish, then r equals 1 when |locations[start] - locations[finish]| <= fuel, and r equals 0 otherwise.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if len(locations) = 2, let d = |locations[0] - locations[1]| and q = floor(fuel / d). If start != finish then r = floor((q + 1) / 2); if start = finish then r = floor(q / 2) + 1.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, consider the two calls count_routes locations start finish fuel and count_routes locations finish start fuel. Whenever these two calls both return results r1 and r2 respectively, r1 = r2.

statement: For every integer k and every slice other with len(other) = len(locations) such that other[i] = locations[i] + k for all 0 <= i < len(locations) and other also satisfies the same location-value constraints, whenever count_routes locations start finish fuel returns r1 and count_routes other start finish fuel returns r2, we have r1 = r2.

statement: For every permutation p of {0, ..., n-1}, where n = len(locations), define other[i] = locations[p(i)] for 0 <= i < n, and let s and f be the indices with p(s) = start and p(f) = finish. Whenever count_routes locations start finish fuel returns r1 and count_routes other s f fuel returns r2, we have r1 = r2.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if start != finish and fuel = |locations[start] - locations[finish]|, let k be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(locations), i != start, i != finish, and min(locations[start], locations[finish]) < locations[i] < max(locations[start], locations[finish]). Then r = (2^k) mod 1000000007.
